html:
Jasenovac was a concentration and extermination camp run from 1941 to 1945 by the Ustaše regime of the Independent State of Croatia, a puppet state of Nazi Germany and Italy.

The Ustaše aimed to rid their state, which included Bosnia, of Serbs, Jews and Roma. At Jasenovac, on the Sava River, prisoners were killed with knives, mallets and guns, or died of hunger and disease. Research puts the number of victims at around 80,000 to 100,000, about half of them Serbs. Communists and Croat opponents also died there. Arguments over the numbers poisoned relations between Serbs and Croats in Yugoslavia and fed the hatreds of the 1990s wars. The site is now a memorial.
sum: Jasenovac was a concentration and extermination camp run from 1941 to 1945 by the Ustaše regime of the Independent State of Croatia, a puppet state of Nazi Germany and Italy.
